Title: Fahmi: Prasarana to operate 24-hour services for National Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: This year's National Day celebration will see Prasarana operate public transport services around the clock on the night of Aug 30 leading into Aug 31, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
"Prasarana has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with National Day.
"We hope this will help more people come to Putrajaya," he said.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after officiating at Majlis Ekspresi Jalur Gemilang JAPEN@Petronas at Petronas NPE Pantai Dalam here.
On Malaysia Day, Fahmi confirmed it would be held at the Borneo Cultural Centre in Kuching, Sarawak — a venue he described as comparable in scale to Penang's PICCA Convention Centre, which hosted last year's celebration.
He said the next planning meeting was scheduled for Aug 24, adding that preparations were progressing well following an initial committee meeting the previous week.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said this year's Jalur Gemilang distribution featured an improved magnet-based design that could be attached to and removed from vehicles, addressing feedback from previous years that motorists preferred a non-permanent option.
"From previous feedback, they prefer magnets over those that are stuck onto the vehicle. So this is an improvement we've made this year," he said.
Fahmi also called on RTM, radio stations and television broadcasters to play the official National Month theme song, 'Aku Berjanji' by Faizal Tahir, more frequently.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangladeshi man held after housemate slashed over misunderstandings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Bangladeshi man who slashed his housemate at a restaurant in Taman Cheras Baru over a series of misunderstandings has been arrested less than 24 hours after the attack.
The suspect, 30, is also a colleague of the victim, a 36-year-old Bangladeshi man.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect was arrested in front of a polyclinic in Kampung Cheras Baru.
"Initial investigations found that the incident stemmed from dissatisfaction and the suspect's inability to control his anger following a series of misunderstandings between the two, who had lived together for five years," he said in a statement.
Rosdi said the victim, who works as a store assistant, was in stable condition at Ampang Hospital.
Police also seized a knife believed to have been used in the attack.
"The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a weapon capable of causing death," he said.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, whipping, or any combination of these punishments.
"We will apply for a remand order against the suspect before a magistrate today," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Afghanistan's gold rush upends lives and landscapes
Article:
AFGHANISTAN: In Afghanistan's northeastern Badakhshan province, dozens of excavators operate day and night to extract gold from the mountains where villagers and their livestock once roamed.
Thousands of miners are deployed across the Shiwa area, about 50 kilometres (30 miles) northeast of the provincial capital Faizabad, extracting gold for investors nationwide.
Some residents in the area have profited from the gold rush, only to regret it later, such as farmer Muhammad Amin.
"Before, the river was deep, the water was clean," said the 74-year-old from Pul-e-Ziri Ban valley.
Since mining got underway, "the water of the river is not drinkable; you can't even wash your body with that water", he told AFP.
With tears in his eyes, Amin said the grass along the riverbank "has all gone" and farming is no longer possible due to "the wind and dust".
Now he can only feed up to 15 goats, compared with as many as 40 previously.
Amin said he was paid half the US$20,000 for which he agreed to lease his land to a mining firm that failed to fulfil a promise to restore his fields after the work stopped.
The Taliban authorities have expanded the mining sector since returning to power five years ago, aiming to tap into Afghanistan's vast underground resources to boost state coffers.
Abdul Mateen Rahimzai, head of Badakhshan's mines department, said they have registered "almost 650 to 700 companies, and there are thousands of people working manually".
The World Bank said hundreds of mining contracts have been signed since 2021, with "real growth averaging 25 to 30 percent" annually according to a May report.
'Better Than Anything Else'
While mining has temporarily stopped in Amin's village, not far from his home, in Gulak-Dara valley, dozens of diggers were carving into the mountainside.
With jobs scarce in Afghanistan, the area has drawn workers from across the country.
Mohammad Agha Khwaja Khail, from Kabul, has worked in mining for five years and earns 10,000 Afghanis (US$150) a month loading trucks.
"It's better than anything else... There aren't many jobs in Kabul," said the 21-year-old, above the din of diggers.
Shafiullah Ehsas, a father-of-five, transported his excavator hundreds of kilometres from Jalalabad about three months ago.
"In Jalalabad, the gold (mining) work hasn't started, and it was happening in Badakhshan, so we didn't have any other option but to bring our machinery here," said the 32-year-old, who earns 25,000 Afghanis per month.
The Ministry of Mines and Petroleum has sought to regulate the industry, with spokesman Hamayoun Afghan saying resources "used to be extracted erratically; it wasn't done under supervision" by the previous government.
Gold mining has accelerated in the north, the ministry spokesman said, including in neighbouring Takhar province where an Afghan company was operating with Chinese partners.
Fabrizio Foschini, a researcher at the Afghanistan Analysts Network, said during earlier decades of war "mining mainly benefited insurgent groups, including the Taliban, and local strongmen with links to corrupt government officials".
Mining firms are now taxed 20 grams of gold per hectare per month, or the equivalent in cash, no matter their profits.
'Reduced to Ruins'
Mohammadullah Mubariz, the manager of a mining company with about a hundred labourers and 20 diggers, said the team can extract "200 to 300 grams of gold" in a week.
Despite this, he said the firm was operating at a loss because of start-up costs since April.
Rahimzai, head of the provincial mines department, said last year the government collected 112 kilograms (247 pounds) of gold in Badakhshan. According to miners who spoke to AFP, their sale price per gram was around US$118.
Rahimzai said that last year, "most of the mines were not registered, and there was no system to collect the fees from them".
He has also ordered the closure of around 225 sites that caused damage, including in the Shiwa area.
"There was a bridge there, there were shops, and there was a school. All of them were buried under floodwater, mud, and debris. The area has been completely reduced to ruins," Rahimzai told AFP.
The provincial mining chief also pledged to tackle any corruption, and ensure the "mineral resources of Badakhshan will be utilised properly and for the benefit of the people".
Some parts of the province remain untouched, including a few kilometres from Shiwa where herder Fazil hoped the miners would stay away.
"Because it's a place for people, for picnics, for livestock to graze," he told AFP, giving only his first name for security reasons.
The gold industry "doesn't benefit the local communities here", said the 45-year-old, who has brought his herd to the mountains each summer since childhood.
"It benefits only the powerful people."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Angklung tunes along Sarawak River strengthen Malaysia Indonesia ties
Article:
KUCHING: The tunes of bamboo angklung were played by about 30 members of the Indonesian Cultural Ambassadors' group during a recent cruise along the Sarawak River.
The music symbolised the close friendship between Malaysia and Indonesia through cultural diplomacy as both countries celebrate their independence month.
The traditional musical instrument of the Sundanese community in West Java was part of a three-day cultural visit to Kuching from Aug 5, held in conjunction with the 81st anniversary of Indonesia's independence.
The programme also provided wider opportunities for cultural exchange and strengthened relations between the people of both countries.
Cahaya Ladara Nusantara general chairperson Triana Wulandari said the visit, organised in collaboration with the Consulate General of the Republic of Indonesia, aimed to introduce Indonesian cultural heritage to the people of Sarawak through angklung performances, traditional dances and batik.
"We are holding a cultural arts goodwill event to introduce and promote Indonesian cultural arts, especially angklung, dance, batik and kebaya to the community in Sarawak in conjunction with the celebration of the Republic of Indonesia's Independence Day.
"Events like this can be a catalyst for stronger cultural ties between Sarawak and Indonesia, thus increasing people-to-people interactions through various artistic activities," she told Bernama.
Triana, 64, who has been involved in culture and history in Indonesia for more than three decades, said art was not just a performance on stage but a universal language that could bring people from different backgrounds closer together.
She said the visit had also opened up opportunities for wider cultural cooperation after the group received an invitation from the Sarawak government to return for a cultural event in Kuching around September or October.
Saung Akar Budaya leader Siti Maryuni Soewardan, who began studying cultural arts while in secondary school, hoped the visit would be the starting point for a cultural exchange programme between Indonesia and Sarawak.
She said cross-cultural programmes should not be limited to artistic performances such as angklung, gamelan and traditional dances, but could also be expanded to include culinary heritage, customs and cultural understanding so that the people of both countries could get to know each other better.
"Angklung itself is not just a traditional musical instrument, but rather a medium that brings together various levels of society from children to the elderly, thus contributing to the physical, mental, social and intellectual well-being of the participants," she said.
Sarawak Tourism Board chief executive officer Dr Sharzede Salleh Askor said the close relationship between Sarawak and Indonesia made cultural exchange an important platform for increasing understanding, especially as both countries celebrated their respective independence months.
She hoped more cultural cooperation programmes between Sarawak and Indonesia would be held in future, strengthening the cultural tourism sector and community relations. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rauf: Elected representatives must understand people's hardships
Article:
MELAKA: Elected representatives in the state have been reminded to remain mindful of the hardships faced by the people, including during floods, and not regard their positions as a privilege.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said those holding elected office had a responsibility to serve all people regardless of race, religion, background or political ideology.
"We do not want to see elected representatives putting on a show, wearing nice clothes and sitting in lavish offices without listening to the rakyat's problems.
"If you want to be an elected representative, you have to be one of the people first.
"You have to understand how difficult it is when floods occur and when there is heavy rain," he said at the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat Parlimen Tangga Batu: Kampung Kita programme here last night.
Rauf said his concern for the people's well-being during bad weather had also led him to constantly monitor the possibility of floods or other untoward incidents.
"When thunder rumbles, I don't sleep because I worry about what might happen the next day.
"It is not easy to organise a special team to monitor whether there are floods, whether anyone has been injured or needs to be rescued, and whether assistance has been provided," he said.
Rauf said this was why he, together with the state leadership and administration, continued to visit villages and residential areas to engage with the community and address their needs.
He said the programme was an important platform for the government to engage with the people regardless of their political affiliations or backgrounds.
"We do not care whether they are Malay, Chinese or Indian, or Muslim, Buddhist, Hindu or Christian.
"Once they are residents of Melaka, they are the people whom we must serve fairly and equitably," he said.
During the programme, Rauf said 531 complaints had been received from the Tangga Batu constituency involving infrastructure, public amenities, housing and welfare issues.
Of these, 343 complaints, or more than 60 per cent, had been resolved, while the remaining 188 were still being followed up by the relevant departments and agencies.
"I want these remaining 188 complaints to be addressed as best as possible. Do not leave the people waiting until they lose hope in us.
"Those that can be resolved, resolve them immediately. For those requiring assistance, we will do our best, while for matters that have yet to be fulfilled, we must continue the struggle until they become a reality, inshaAllah," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fijian foreign and external trade minister visits Malaysia to strengthen ties
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fijian Foreign and External Trade Minister, Sakiasi Raisevu Ditoka, will undertake a working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to Wednesday to further strengthen bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Fiji.
Malaysia's Foreign Ministry in a statement said during the visit, Ditoka will meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss efforts to further strengthen bilateral cooperation between the two countries, particularly in trade and investment, capacity building, forestry, renewable energy, and culture.
"The meeting will also provide an opportunity for both ministers to exchange views on regional and international issues, as well as strengthen cooperation with the Pacific Island countries," the statement read.
Ditoka is also scheduled to meet Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani to explore new opportunities in economic cooperation for the mutual benefits of the two countries.
During the visit, the minister will officiate the reopening of the High Commission of the Republic of Fiji in Kuala Lumpur and the establishment of the Malaysia-Fiji Business Council, the ministry added.
In 2025, total bilateral trade between Malaysia and Fiji amounted to RM880.01 million (US$206.2 million), with Malaysia's exports valued at RM867.92 million (US$203.41 million) and imports from Fiji valued at RM12.09 million (US$2.80 million).

Title: Johari: Malaysia must not open market faster than local industries can adapt
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Malaysia must avoid opening its market to foreign competition faster than domestic industries can adapt, particularly when local companies are up against much larger players with significant economies of scale.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said foreign investment should complement local industries by bringing in technology and capabilities Malaysia lacks, rather than displacing businesses built up over decades.
Citing the iron and steel industry, Johari said Malaysia had developed it over decades, but local players subsequently struggled after the market was opened to much larger foreign producers with significantly greater production capacity.
"Our market is not big. When you open the market so fast, when we are not ready, this is what we face," he said in his officiating speech at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia's 80th annual general meeting.
"While these investments expanded production capacity, the structural challenge they were intended to address remained unresolved as imports of iron and steel products increased over the past 10 years.
"If new investments develop in isolation from local firms or compete directly without creating meaningful industrial linkages, domestic capabilities can gradually weaken, putting local firms out of business," he said.
Johari said Malaysian entrepreneurs had built their businesses over the years through perseverance and continuous reinvestment, with many starting as traders before expanding into manufacturing and exports.
"We cannot allow future industrial policies to reverse that progress. If we are not careful, Malaysia risks becoming merely a marketplace for foreign products, and our businesses will regress and become traders only, once again.
"Our responsibility is to ensure that we leave behind stronger industrial capabilities, not fewer, for the next generation," he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Johari said the government would continue to welcome foreign investors but would take greater care to ensure their investments did not directly undermine existing Malaysian businesses.
He said the government would assess the nature of an investor's business, including what it produced and where it sourced its raw materials, when processing licence applications.
"That is why, when we process licences, we will look at what sort of business the investor is involved in, where they source their raw materials and what they intend to do. This allows us to engage with the relevant associations.
"For example, this morning, we met with ACCCIM and discussed what they thought about this. We asked whether they thought the investment would affect their businesses or complement them. These are the things we need to look at," he told reporters.
Johari said Malaysia should leverage foreign investment to address technology gaps by encouraging investors to bring in new technologies and partner with established local companies rather than displacing them.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EC to prepare updated report on Sarawak bid for 17 new seats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Election Commission (EC) to prepare an updated report on Sarawak's proposal to add 17 new state assembly seats, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
Ministers Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri and Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi raised the matter at a recent cabinet meeting, he said.
"This was raised in a recent cabinet meeting, and the prime minister has requested the Election Commission to prepare an updated report on this matter so that we can implement it.
"The prime minister's commitment is to implement it," he said.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after officiating at Majlis Ekspresi Jalur Gemilang JAPEN@Petronas at Petronas NPE Pantai Dalam here.
However, Fahmi said no timeline had been established as the cabinet was still awaiting further input from the EC.
"Not yet — the cabinet has not been updated on that yet because we are waiting on a few matters from the EC," he said.
Previously, an online portal reported that Nancy and Nanta had brought the matter to the cabinet, pressing for the federal government to advance the redelineation process so it could be brought before Parliament for endorsement.
Nancy said she and Nanta were aware that the EC had already completed the necessary procedures on its end, and that the Sarawak government had given its approval, leaving the federal stage as the remaining step.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAP urges crackdown on motorists vaping behind the wheel
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Road users could face growing risks from motorists vaping while driving unless the government takes decisive action to curb the practice, says the Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP).
Its education officer N.V. Subbarow said the association had received numerous complaints about motorists, including express bus and lorry drivers and motorcyclists, vaping on the road.
He said the practice was particularly concerning as some
vape liquids could contain synthetic drugs
that impair users and affect their judgement behind the wheel.
"Even older people vape while driving because they believe it keeps them alert. But who is checking whether they are actually impaired?
"Non-smokers and non-vapers should not become victims because someone chooses to vape while driving," he told the New Straits Times today.
Subbarow called for strict enforcement against motorists caught vaping or using drug-laced vape products while driving, including hefty compounds and, for serious or repeat offences, suspension or disqualification of driving licences.
He cited Singapore's tougher approach to vaping as a model Malaysia should consider.
His call comes amid growing concern over the misuse of electronic cigarettes as a vehicle for synthetic drugs.
Police have warned that products marketed as "Piu Piu" and "Magic Mushroom" are commercial terms for synthetic liquid drugs used in vape devices, with authorities investigating possible links to road accidents.
As of April, Malaysia had recorded 402 cases involving vape products containing dangerous synthetic drugs, including benzodiazepines, MDMA, THC and methamphetamine, according to Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
Police have also detected fentanyl being sold in vape liquids, with a nationwide operation resulting in significant drug seizures and arrests earlier this year.
Subbarow said CAP believed stronger enforcement was necessary as some motorists may regard vaping as legal and see little reason to stop while driving.
He urged the Health Ministry and other relevant agencies to consider a total ban on vape and electronic cigarette products as soon as possible.
"Unless the government takes a drastic decision on vaping, we may continue to see more road safety concerns involving motorists who use these products," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2 Mercedes-Benz seized after businessmen 'forget' road tax, insurance
Article:
KLANG: Two businessmen had their Mercedes-Benz cars seized by the Road Transport Department (RTD) after the luxury vehicles were found to have no valid road tax or insurance coverage.
Selangor RTD director Datuk Ahmad Kamarunzaman Mehat said both men were stopped during Ops Luxury at Taman Berkeley and the Federal Highway.
Checks found that the licences for both cars had expired around May and that the vehicles had no valid insurance.
"They claimed the cars were rarely driven because they had other vehicles, causing them to forget to renew the licences.
"Both cars have been impounded at the Shah Alam RTD headquarters," he said in a statement.
Kamarunzaman said members of the public could report traffic offences to aduantrafik@jpj.gov.my or through the e-Aduan app, together with the complainant's and offence details.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean at 59: Bolstering centrality from within as bloc advances Vision 2045
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (Asean) marked its 59th anniversary yesterday, the bloc finds itself at a pivotal time as it navigates new geopolitical realities reshaping the region.
Having demonstrated success and resilience for nearly six decades and established its international standing, Asean's challenge is no longer simply about proving its relevance.
Rather, analysts said for the 11-member association, strengthening internal unity and regional integration is now more crucial than ever as both will be key to preserving ASEAN's centrality and resilience amid rising geopolitical competition and complex regional challenges.
The United States (US)-Iran war and wider conflict in West Asia have exposed the region to energy security concerns and disruptions in global trade and supply chains.
There is impetus now for ASEAN to harness its growing diplomatic influence and deliver real benefits for its 700 million peoples, as the bloc charts its future under the ASEAN Community Vision 2045.
International Islamic University Malaysia's (IIUM) Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS) Director, Prof Dr Phar Kim Beng, said Asean's future ultimately depends not only on recognition by external partners of its centrality and reassurance that they respect the bloc's role and position in the region, but also on its ability to close ranks and reinforce its centrality from within.
"Ideally, Asean member states themselves have to insist on it, that Asean is always a central and pivotal actor as a grouping.
"Asean also has to do a lot of work to make sure that it does really become what it aspires to be, which is a single economic community that is strong, vibrant," Phar, who was a former Asean Secretariat official, told Bernama.
He said greater efforts are required to enhance labour mobility, digital connectivity, and government-to-government cooperation among member states.
Meanwhile, Jawaharlal Nehru University's (JNU) Centre for Indo-Pacific Studies Associate Professor, Dr Rahul Mishra, said while Asean has shown considerable normative appeal in managing internal and external challenges, more still needs to be done to safeguard its centrality and strategic interests.
The growing competition between the US and China, and the fast-escalating South China Sea dispute, pose tremendous challenges, and Asean must now match its increasing diplomatic influence with stronger practical and functional cooperation with its partners.
Asean's recently expanded its external engagement to 12 partners, following an elevation of Turkiye's status to a full dialogue partner.
The Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia (TAC) which marks its 50th year this year, also saw the number of High Contracting Parties rise to 62 from 58, following the accession of Sweden, Poland, Romania, and Lithuania last month.
"Asean must move beyond the realm of dialogues and intent to work with its partners and focus on translating its promises into action, especially in intra-regional and regional security domains, seamless physical and digital connectivity, regional economic integration, dispute resolution, and in managing relations with superpowers" he said.
Additionally, he said, the Myanmar crisis and growing threat of cyber scams emanating from the region must be dealt with in a more resolute, coordinated, and time-bound manner.
"Unless Asean addresses these pressing regional challenges head-on, it would be difficult for the organisation to remain relevant in regional security dynamics," he added.
Established on Aug 8, 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, Asean has since expanded to a total 11 members following the inclusion of Brunei in 1984, Vietnam (1995), Laos (1997), Myanmar (1997), and Cambodia (1999). Timor-Leste, its newest member, was admitted during the 47th Asean Summit in October last year.
This year's Asean Day celebration was held under the theme "Navigating Our Future Together," which is also the theme of Asean 2026 under the chairmanship of the Philippines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver's failure to engage 'P' gear led to KKIA SUV crash — Police
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: An SUV is believed to have moved on its own after its driver apparently failed to engage the 'P' (park) gear before crashing through the glass doors of the Departure Hall at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) on Friday.
The incident occurred at about 4.55pm when the 66-year-old woman stopped in the second lane outside the terminal to pick up her child.
Kota Kinabalu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Shahrudin Mat Husain said preliminary investigations found that the woman had apparently failed to engage the 'P' gear while preparing to switch drivers.
He said the SUV began moving slowly as she was getting out, causing her to panic and accidentally press the accelerator.
"This caused the vehicle to accelerate and collide with another vehicle.
"The SUV then veered off course and crashed through the glass doors of the KKIA departure area before hitting a pillar," he said in a statement today.
Shahrudin said the woman managed to get out of the SUV before the collision but suffered minor facial injuries from shattered glass.
She was taken by ambulance to Queen Elizabeth Hospital I for treatment.
He said the case was being investigated under Rule 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959 [LN 166/59], under the Road Transport Act 1987.
Shahrudin advised motorists to ensure their vehicles were safely secured before leaving them unattended and to drive carefully and responsibly.
The incident attracted public attention after videos and photographs of the SUV inside the departure hall were circulated on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 76 illegal dumpsites remain active in Selangor
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor has identified 76 illegal dumpsites that remain active as the state government steps up efforts to curb illegal dumping.
Selangor Local Government and Tourism Committee chairman Datuk Ng Suee Lim said the state government was adopting an approach covering prevention, monitoring, cleanup and enforcement.
He said the current priority was addressing the 76 active sites, particularly repeat or identified hotspot locations, through more frequent monitoring, cleanup operations and enforcement by local authorities and related agencies.
"At the same time, the state government is expanding the use of closed-circuit television cameras at illegal dumping hotspots to help with monitoring and detecting offences, alongside strengthening integrated action between local authorities, KDEB Waste Management, district land offices and related enforcement agencies," he said.
"The state government's approach is not just about cleaning up rubbish after it has been dumped. Our focus is to break the cycle of illegal dumping so that cleaned-up locations do not turn back into illegal dumpsites," he told Harian Metro.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ngeh dismisses claims DAP reps staying in govt for posts, pay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A senior DAP leader has dismissed claims that the party's representatives want to remain in government to keep the perks and salaries that come with their ministerial posts.
"I regard those claims as baseless," said DAP national treasurer Ngeh Koo Ham in an interview with Berita Harian.
"The salaries of all DAP ministers are cut by 20 per cent. They also have to contribute part of their salaries to DAP and their respective states," he said, adding the contributions are subject to tax.
Ngeh said DAP ministers and members of parliament worked very hard, and that there have been no corruption allegations against them.
"Ultimately, the question of whether DAP should remain in government must be decided by party members. About 4,000 delegates will attend and have the right to determine the party's direction," he said, on the coming DAP congress.
Next week's DAP congress will see delegates decide whether the party's representatives should remain in government.
"That is why, to me, the decision on DAP's future in government must be made democratically and transparently by party members themselves.
"Most importantly, the purpose of remaining in government is to continue serving the people, not for self-interest."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah waters exploited as transit routes for cross-border drug syndicates
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Cross-border drug syndicates are exploiting Sabah's vast maritime frontier, including waters off Semporna and Tawau, as transit points to move methamphetamine and other drugs between Malaysia and neighbouring countries.
Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director-general Maritime Admiral Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said the syndicates were taking advantage of hundreds of small islands, secluded jetties, long coastlines and traditional sea routes to evade detection.
According to a Sinar Harian report, he said the areas were being used as temporary transit points or "drop-off" locations, where drugs were left before being collected by other members of the syndicate at a different time.
"This layered method is intended to make detection more difficult as each individual in the chain only knows a small part of the overall operation.
"The method demonstrates a high level of coordination between local and foreign networks, proving that this is organised cross-border crime.
"For the island modus operandi, it does exist, but we see that the quantities are not large, only moderate or smaller.
"If the quantity of drugs is large, the syndicate will deal directly with the recipient because it involves delivery and payment.
"For example, if 50kg of drugs are being transported, the drugs have to reach the recipient for payment to be made.
"Leaving the drugs on an island carries risks, including the drugs being stolen, taken by a third party or seized by the authorities.
"Most of these risks are reduced by the smugglers," he said.
For large-scale smuggling operations, Rosli said syndicates used commercial vessels to evade the authorities.
He said the main challenge was no longer understanding the modus operandi but identifying which vessels were being used in smuggling operations.
More than 100,000 vessels pass through the Strait of Malacca each year, making detection dependent on strong intelligence gathering and cooperation between multiple countries.
He cited the success of the MMEA Pahang operation in February, which seized about 1.5 tonnes of methamphetamine worth more than RM78.6 million after intercepting two vessels near the Pahang-Terengganu maritime border.
The operation also resulted in the arrest of 18 crew members, including two vessel captains.
"Detection methods vary, but the most important are intelligence and thorough inspections. In certain situations, we also use the services of the police K9 Unit and drug-detection technology," he said.
Rosli said Malaysia was not a drug-producing country but was being used as a transit country and destination.
He said Malaysian waters continued to be targeted by cross-border syndicates taking advantage of the country's strategic position along regional maritime routes.
The threat also involved Sabah, which has an extensive maritime border with the Philippines and Indonesia.
In the northern peninsula, syndicates have been detected using high-powered fibre boats and wooden boats to bring in methamphetamine, "yaba" pills and cannabis through ship-to-ship transfers to prevent the identities of suppliers and recipients from being detected.
In the south, waters off Selangor, Melaka and Johor have been identified as among the main routes for smuggling drugs from abroad.
Intelligence indicated that supplies would be delivered to designated meeting points before being collected by other syndicate networks, reflecting an organised criminal logistics system.
Rosli said syndicates also used various types of boats, including bot pancung, bot pom-pom, high-powered fibre boats and speedboats commonly used for fishing or daily maritime transportation.
The drugs were concealed alongside other goods to avoid detection before being handed over to the next network.
"This tactic allows smuggling to be carried out covertly before the supplies are handed over to syndicate networks at predetermined locations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran issues demands for reopening of Hormuz
Article:
DUBAI: Iran set preconditions on Saturday for a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, including compensation for war damages, complicating a potential deal to open the waterway essential to the world economy.
Teheran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel struck Iran in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage, attacking ships it accuses of attempting to circumvent its preferred route.
Continued attacks in the strait, which was free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire. Mediators have since urged both sides to return to the terms of a June memorandum.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said discussions with Oman over transit and management of the strait were "approaching the final stages", but added the reopening of Hormuz "is subject to other conditions and compensation for the violation" of the June agreement.
Security chief Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr on Saturday laid out a list of demands for reopening the strait, including an end to the "war and aggression against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen, and Iraq."
He also demanded the lifting of a parallel US naval blockade of Iran, the end of sanctions, the release of frozen assets and compensation for wartime damage, according to remarks reported by Tasnim news agency.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said Hormuz's reopening had "nothing to do with the negotiations between Iran and Oman", adding that the "enemy is forced to accept Iran's conditions for the opening of the strait."
The comments came as transit through Hormuz has dropped significantly, with Iran targeting ships it accuses of skirting its preferred route through Iranian waters.
The United Arab Emirates' foreign ministry on Saturday condemned what it called a "hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company) with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties."
Later on Saturday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a ship was hit by a projectile off Oman in the Strait of Hormuz, causing a fire that was extinguished but no casualties. It was unclear whether they were referring to the same ship.
On Friday, ADNOC had put out a statement saying that since the start of the war, 15 of its vessels had been attacked in Hormuz, "including three vessels this week alone."
Oman's foreign ministry on Saturday condemned "repeated attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz", without naming Iran.
It also said that "ongoing negotiations regarding navigation arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz are proceeding in a positive and constructive atmosphere", and urged against any actions that might jeopardise the progress.
The previous Iran-US deal – meant to serve as a jumping-off point for negotiations on a permanent settlement – had said Iran and Oman would hash out future arrangements for the strait in discussion with other Gulf countries and "in line with the applicable international law."
International law generally forbids tolling in such waterways.
Turkiye's foreign minister said Saturday he expected Egypt to join a joint defence agreement between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan designed to stabilise the region, calling the country a "natural partner on all issues."
"I believe that at the next stage Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members," Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said in an interview.
A drone struck US assets at an Egyptian port on the Mediterranean last month, marking the first drone attack on Egyptian territory since the outbreak of the Iran war.
Fidan said the agreement does not target a specific country.
"There is no common threat that we have put in writing," he said, according to the news agency.
Pakistan's foreign ministry said Friday the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was "intended to strengthen collective deterrence."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japanese cuisine to boost Japan's agricultural and seafood product exports to Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Japanese cuisine, driven by demand for halal food products and rising consumer incomes, will boost exports of Japanese agricultural and seafood products to Malaysia, said Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) Kuala Lumpur managing director Koichi Takano.
"Malaysia now ranks 10th among all export destinations for Japanese agricultural, forestry, fishery, and food products, improving from 13th place previously.
"This underscores Malaysia's growing importance as a key market for Japan in Southeast Asia and reflects the continued growth in demand for Japanese food products among Malaysian consumers and businesses," he told Bernama in an interview during the Japanese Cuisine Lecture Series organised by Jetro recently at Taylor's University.
He said awareness of the cultural significance of Washoku, or traditional Japanese cuisine, which was inscribed on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013, has also boosted demand.
Takano noted that statistics from the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries showed that Japan's exports of agricultural, forestry, fishery and food products to Malaysia reached 29.1 billion yen (100 yen=RM2.60)  in 2025, a 26.3 per cent increase year-on-year compared with 2024.
"The data indicate that agricultural products accounted for about 70 per cent of total exports, while seafood products accounted for about 29 per cent.
"The total value of Japan's exports of agricultural, forestry, fishery and food products to Malaysia reached 15 billion yen during the period from January to May 2026, a 42.3 per cent increase compared with the same period in 2025," Takano said.
He said e-commerce and demand generated from travel to Japan have also provided a platform to spur demand for Japanese cuisine.
"The increase in Japanese restaurants globally demonstrates that Japanese cuisine has become well established internationally," he remarked.
Kyodo News reported that Japan's exports of agricultural, forestry and fishery products and food products in the first half of 2026 rose 10.9 per cent from a year earlier to 897.7 billion yen (US$5.7 billion), a record high for the period, according to the Japanese government.
Green tea posted a notable gain, supported by a global matcha boom, with the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries saying that growing inbound tourism has raised overseas awareness of Japanese food, according to the Tokyo-based news agency.
Malaysia as a Gateway for the Expansion of Japanese Food Products
Across the Asean region, he said, Malaysia has strong potential as a gateway for the expansion of Japanese food culture and products.
"It is a multiracial, multicultural market that is well accustomed to diverse culinary traditions and international food offerings.
"The country also benefits from the widespread use of English, a well-developed network of international hotels, food manufacturers, and educational institutions, as well as established halal certification systems, food processing capabilities, and logistics infrastructure," he emphasised.
Takano outlined a successful Malaysian model that integrates human resource development, product innovation, halal readiness, and efficient distribution networks that could serve as a valuable framework for promoting Japanese cuisine and food products across Asean and other Muslim-majority markets.
He also pointed to the need to identify authentic Japanese food products with key tools such as trademarks, geographical indications (GIs) and country-of-origin labelling, to avoid counterfeit products.
"Producers and companies should also register their intellectual property rights in export markets, establish authorised distribution channels and improve product traceability throughout the supply chain," Takano said.
He also emphasised that applying Japanese culinary techniques to fresh Malaysian ingredients can create a more sustainable and commercially viable business model that also benefits local producers in Malaysia.
"The overall outlook remains positive and we expect more Japanese companies to establish food service businesses and operations in the coming years," he said.
On the impact of a weaker yen on the food service industry in Malaysia, Takano said, a weaker Japanese currency does not automatically result in lower prices of all Japanese food products, especially as Japanese producers continue to face rising costs associated with fertiliser, animal feed, energy, packaging materials, imported raw materials and logistics.
As for extreme weather conditions, such as El Niño, he said, while they could have an impact on farming in Japan and exports, they do not affect every agricultural product or seafood equally.
The effects of higher temperatures, low rainfall, excessive rainfall or pests, he explained, vary significantly by crop, geographical location and growing season.
"Potential risks can be mitigated through measures such as diversifying sourcing regions, adopting improved farming practices, investing in freezing and processing technologies, and maintaining effective inventory management," he added.
As part of Jetro's role in promoting exports of Japanese food products in Malaysia, Takano said the organisation is conducting a lecture series on Japanese cuisine, in collaboration with Taylor's University, for aspiring chefs who will lead the next generation of Malaysia's food service industry in hotels and restaurants.
"This initiative is not only a short-term promotional activity but a strategic, long-term investment in nurturing future demand and strengthening the presence of Japanese food in Malaysia," Takano shared.
In the future, he said, similar collaboration with other universities, culinary and hospitality institutions could be explored to further expand Japanese cuisine in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar, Wan Azizah visit Fadillah and Ismail Sabri at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof at the National Heart Institute (IJN) yesterday.
Anwar said Fadillah was recovering well but still needed rest following his heart bypass surgery.
"Alhamdulillah, his health is improving," he said in a social media post.
During the visit, the couple also called on former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is receiving treatment and undergoing a procedure for an irregular heartbeat.
Anwar said he and Dr Wan Azizah prayed for a speedy recovery for both leaders, wishing them continued strength and good health to serve the nation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4,000 Myanmar nationals in immigration depots to undergo refugee screening
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department and police have begun screening Myanmar nationals held at immigration depots to determine their refugee status, says Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said authorities had identified about 4,000 Myanmar nationals currently held at immigration depots, stressing that this did not mean all had refugee status.
"To determine whether they are refugees or Myanmar nationals who have committed offences under the Immigration Act and other laws, we need to screen them," he said at the Star City FC Tour Send-off Ceremony at Putrajaya Square here.
On Wednesday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said that repatriation would proceed with certain considerations, as Malaysia would not return
Myanmar refugees
if their lives were at risk.
He said Wisma Putra and the Home Ministry were still assessing the proposed plan.
Saifuddin said Malaysia's Myanmar refugee population comprised 19 ethnic groups, including the Chin and Arakanese, and cautioned against framing the issue solely around the Rohingya.
"That's why I've directed the Immigration Department and police to begin this data collection process.
"It's happening now. They will report the numbers to me from time to time.
"If they are confirmed to be refugees, they will certainly be among the first group we manage for repatriation. That will be handled by the Foreign Ministry.
"I can't speak on behalf of the Foreign Ministry. Our job is to carry out the data collection," he said.
Saifuddin said not all Myanmar nationals covered by the exercise were in detention, with some believed to be at large.
He said the government would need a mechanism to reach out to them and encourage them to come forward for the data collection exercise.
"I expect the first set of data to be ready in the fourth quarter of this year. It's already August. Whatever the numbers turn out to be, I will share them with the media then," he said.
Last month, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Myanmar had agreed to accept an
initial group
of 5,000 of its nationals currently in Malaysia following negotiations between the two governments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China July factory-gate inflation eases to three-month low, CPI slows
Article:
BEIJING: China's producer price inflation eased more than expected in July to its weakest in three months, while consumer inflation also cooled, official data showed on Sunday, as global energy prices retreated despite the US-Israel war against Iran.
China's leaders, confronting a two-speed economy of strong factory output and exports but weak domestic demand, have pledged to bolster growth by accelerating fiscal spending on already budgeted infrastructure projects through year-end.
"Lower oil prices, combined with weakening demand, caused both (consumer and producer price inflation) in July to come in below expectations. Oil price trends remain uncertain, meaning their impact on inflation is also likely to be uncertain," said Zhaopeng Xing, ANZ's senior China strategist.
"On the demand side, the effect of faster fiscal spending in the second half of the year is likely to be felt with a lag of about one quarter. We maintain our view that inflation will follow an M-shaped trajectory this year."
FISCAL LAG, LIMITED EFFECT ON QUELLING PRICE WARS
The producer price index (PPI) rose 3.5 per cent from a year earlier in July, National Bureau of Statistics data showed, easing from 4.1 per cent in June to its lowest in three months. It was below economists' expectations for a 3.8 per cent increase in a Reuters poll.
The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile costs for food and energy, rose 0.9 per cent on year, food prices fell 1.5 per cet. From the previous month, CPI edged down 0.1 per cent, compared with an expected 0.2 per cent gain and following a 0.3 per cent dip in June.
Zhiwei Zhang, chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, said the slower inflation was consistent with other activity data such as the PMI reading.
"The economic momentum softened in Q2," Zhang said. "The Politburo in July signalled stronger fiscal spending as the policy response. The transmission of the fiscal spending will take time."
ANZ forecasts full-year PPI of 2.5 per cent and CPI of one per cent.
Although some of China's upstream and high-tech sectors have maintained strong profit growth, more domestic market-facing manufacturers struggled against sluggish demand as overall economic growth lost steam. Rising input costs risk further squeezing their profit margins and dampening confidence.
Higher producer prices were driven mainly by increases in the mining and raw materials sectors, the statistics agency said. By contrast, prices declined for food and daily consumer goods.
Price shocks stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the key oil and gas passage, have lifted producer prices and helped flip China's years-long deflationary streak.
Government efforts to curb fierce price wars in major industrial sectors and stabilise prices had previously achieved only limited effects.
With household demand for goods still subdued by a property market slump and low job security, deflationary pressures likely remained, economists say.
Factory activity contracted in July in an official survey and slowed to a four-month low in a private-sector survey, with both data sets showing weakening new orders.
China's top leaders, at a key meeting in late July, signalled stronger support for the economy and vowed to continue cracking down on competition—price wars among manufacturers chasing market share at the expense of profits.
They also pledged to introduce pragmatic and effective new policies in a timely manner, and more forcefully expand domestic demand and improve supply.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Near collision' at Sydney Airport triggers investigation
Article:
SYDNEY: Safety regulators launched an investigation on Sunday into a "near collision" between two passenger aircraft at Australia's busiest airport that injured a crew member.
The incident, which involved a Jetstar pilot being forced to apply sudden brakes to avoid crashing into a Qatar Airways jet on Sunday morning, disrupted operations at Sydney Airport.
The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) said a Jetstar Airbus A320 was taxiing for a flight to the Gold Coast on Sunday morning when its crew "observed a Qatar Airways Boeing 777, under tow from an aircraft tug, in close proximity on a crossing taxiway."
"A cabin crew member aboard the [Jetstar] A320 was injured, and there was damage to the connection between the 777 nose gear and aircraft tug" as both planes stopped abruptly, the statement said.
Investigators are collecting data from both aircraft, air traffic control, and interviewing crew and tug operators to determine the cause of the near collision, the regulator said.
It called for witnesses at the airport to send in any video of the near collision.
Flights at Sydney Airport are experiencing delays after the incident, Airservices Australia said.
"Our aircraft was following instructions by Air Traffic Control when the pilots were forced to brake firmly after another aircraft came in close proximity," said a Jetstar spokeswoman.
A Jetstar crew member moving through the cabin was injured when the plane abruptly stopped, and later treated by paramedics.
Qatar Airways did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
An official not authorised to speak publicly said early information suggested the tug pulling the Qatar plane did not follow air traffic control instructions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,524 wild animal attacks since 2020 leave 54 dead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) recorded 1,524 human-wildlife conflict cases between 2020 and July this year.
Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the incidents resulted in 1,470 injuries and 54 fatalities.
He attributed the conflicts to shrinking natural habitats, land clearing, and development projects, which led to habitat fragmentation.
"These conditions force wildlife to seek new roaming areas near forests, plantations, and neighbouring villages.
"In addition, members of the public feeding wildlife, particularly primates, encourages conflicts between humans and monkeys," he said, adding that poor waste management was also a contributing factor.
Kadir said high breeding rates among primates led to annual population growth, as the species were highly adaptable with strong survival capabilities.
"Increased public awareness of wildlife conflict and easier access to mass media and departmental complaint platforms have strengthened the government's ability to receive comprehensive reports from the public."
In some cases, he said Perhilitan was moving away from complete reliance on catch-and-relocate methods, which were costly, and focusing on modern mitigation measures, including GPS satellite collars.
These are fitted on wild elephant herd leaders to monitor their movements in real time, triggering early warning systems when herds approach plantation or residential boundaries.
Kadir said patrol units also used thermal drones to safely detect wildlife, such as elephants or tigers, in dense brush before the animals entered villages.
"Camera traps, meanwhile, monitor intrusion hotspots to gather behavioural data for early control measures."
He called on the public to report any disturbances involving wildlife via the Perhilitan hotline at 1-800-88-5151 or its e-Aduan portal, and avoid taking matters into their own hands.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Animal rights group urges probe into puppy death
Article:
Animal rights group urges probe into puppy death
New Straits Times
KUALA LUMPUR: Police and relevant authorities have been urged to treat the death of a puppy allegedly struck twice by a vehicle as an urgent animal cruelty case and not allow it to become another routine file.
Lawyers for Animal Rights representative Rajesh Nagarajan said CCTV footage in the vicinity should be secured and preserved before it was lost or overwritten, while the white Mitsubishi Triton allegedly involved should be identified and traced without delay.
Rajesh said the incident, as described in a police report lodged at the Lukut Police Station, involved the vehicle striking a white puppy before allegedly hitting it a second time, resulting in its death.
"We do not accept that this can be dismissed as a momentary lapse of attention, an act of negligence or an unfortunate accident.
"The facts, as reported, point to something else entirely: a deliberate act of cruelty," he said in a statement.
Rajesh said what made the case particularly troubling was the alleged second impact involving the same animal.
He called for the case to be investigated and prosecuted under the Animal Welfare Act 2015, with the person responsible swiftly identified and arrested and prosecuted to the fullest extent permitted by law.
"Any attempt to reduce this case to a mere property offence under the Penal Code would, in our view, be a serious mischaracterisation of the law and a betrayal of the legislative intent behind the Animal Welfare Act," he said.
He also urged authorities to obtain a veterinary forensic report to establish the precise cause of death and corroborate the account of a second impact.
Rajesh said statements should also be taken from all available witnesses, including those who arrived at the scene after the incident.
Earlier, a video went viral showing a puppy lying on the road before the driver of the Mitsubishi Triton appeared to drive over the animal.
The driver then reversed the vehicle and appeared to run over the puppy a second time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Melaka polls: PKR, BN in talks, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR is in discussions with all parties ahead of the Melaka election, including Barisan Nasional (BN), says party information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had expressed openness to cross-party engagement, which PKR welcomed.
"Datuk Seri Rauf, the Chief Minister, has expressed openness to discussing with any party. So, we welcome this," he said, adding that Melaka PKR acting chairman Adam Adli had held several preliminary discussions.
Fahmi was speaking to reporters after officiating the Majlis Ekspresi Jalur Gemilang JAPEN@Petronas at Petronas NPE Pantai Dalam here.
He said the party's preparations were progressing despite no dissolution date having been set for the state assembly.
"Preparations at the party level involve identifying candidates, seats and holding discussions with all parties, including our colleagues in BN," he said.
Fahmi also welcomed BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's statement that the coalition was ready to discuss seat arrangements for Melaka and at federal level ahead of the next general election.
He said PKR had tasked vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution, who is currently acting deputy president, and election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari with leading the inter-party discussions.
Last month,
Pakatan Harapan (PH) withdrew its support for Rauf
after the state assembly passed the Melaka State Constitution (Amendment) Enactment 2026, allowing up to seven unelected members to be appointed to the assembly.
Meanwhile, Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said he had directed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to coordinate with the Election Commission (EC) to identify and address Internet connectivity needs at polling centres across Melaka.
He said MCMC had ensured near-complete Internet access at polling centres in Johor and Negri Sembilan and would seek to replicate that standard in Melaka.
"MCMC in Johor and Negri Sembilan ensured that almost every polling centre had satisfactory internet access. We will do the same for Melaka by preparing the necessary internet services," he said.
The Melaka state assembly's current term expires on Dec 30, with an election required by late February 2027.
BN currently controls 21 of the 28 seats in the assembly.
PH was invited to join the Melaka government following the formation of the unity government at federal level, but the arrangement collapsed in July.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Residents fume over nightly smoke from illegal dumpsite
Article:
DENGKIL: Residents here have been enduring smoke from open burning at an illegal dumpsite almost every night since 2022, with some claiming the fumes have caused breathing difficulties and posed a health risk.
Kita Cybersouth Community Association representative Hadi Osman, 43, said he became aware of the dumpsite, about 600m from his home, after moving to the area in 2022.
"Since moving here in 2022, residents have had to endure the smell of smoke from open burning at the illegal dumpsite almost every night, to the point that it causes breathing difficulties and threatens our health," he told Metro Ahad.
Hadi said lorries believed to be carrying waste entered the privately owned land almost daily at about 5pm, 9pm and midnight.
"The waste would then be burned at about 2am every day to get rid of the evidence.
"Residents have lodged numerous complaints with the authorities and made police reports, but the illegal dumpsite has yet to be resolved," he said.
He said residents were also afraid to confront those responsible after being told the area was controlled by a secret society.
"The latest incident occurred yesterday (Friday), when the area caught fire, forcing residents to contact the Fire and Rescue Department as the blaze spread to nearby areas," he said.
Meanwhile, Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant state director of operations Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 3.08am on Friday.
He said a Fire Rescue Tender from the Cyberjaya Fire and Rescue Station, with seven personnel, was dispatched and arrived at the scene at 3.14am.
"Upon arrival, firefighters found a bush fire near the Cybersouth Roundabout.
"Firefighting operations were carried out using a single hose line supplied with water from the fire engine's tank until the fire was completely extinguished.
"The team then conducted an overhaul to ensure there were no remaining sources that could cause the fire to reignite," he said in a statement yesterday.
Ashrul said the fire was brought under control at 3.20am, with operations ending at 3.28am. No casualties were reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia closes all access to Mount Bromo as wildfire expands
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia has closed Mount Bromo national park in East Java for all tourist activities, its operator said late on Saturday, as a wildfire, burning since Monday, expanded in its caldera area.
* The closure took effect from Saturday evening, for an undetermined duration, the park operator said on its official Instagram page.
The raging fire has burned an area of around 176 hectares (434.91 acres) at Mount Bromo, an active volcano that is a popular tourist destination known for its "sand sea" caldera.
The wildfire has expanded from around 60 hectares on Thursday.
"This closure is a crucial step to maintain safety of visitors, staff and people in the surrounding areas," it said, adding that people who have bought entrance tickets will be able to reschedule visits or seek a refund.
East Java's disaster mitigation agency said authorities are deploying water bombing helicopters and water spraying drones to bolster efforts to extinguish the fire.
Footage uploaded by the park's operator on social media showed fire spreading across the slopes of the mountain overnight.
Authorities have not declared what caused the fire, and there have been no casualties reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Marzuki slams PN for questioning Bersatu's 'moral courage'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former aide to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has hit out at Perikatan Nasional after one of its leaders insinuated that the party lacked "moral courage".
Datuk Dr Marzuki Mohamad said Bersatu, which Muhyiddin leads, had the right to question its position in PN in line with the coalition's constitution, which must be respected by all parties.
"Bersatu was said to have automatically lost its membership in PN when it contested using its own logo and announced the formation of a new coalition in the recent Negri Sembilan election.
"However, there is not a single clause in the PN Constitution that provides for the automatic termination of a component party's membership.
"So, there is no need to talk about 'moral courage' because your action against Bersatu was completely immoral and unconstitutional," he said in a Facebook post.
Marzuki was believed to be responding to comments by PN information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa.
Yesterday, without naming any party, Annuar said certain parties should have the "moral courage" to accept that their actions led to the loss of their membership in PN.
In his post, Marzuki questioned PN's ability to govern the country fairly and equitably if rights enshrined in its own constitution were not respected.
Separately, Marzuki claimed Bersatu was barred from attending the PN Supreme Council meeting to discuss seat allocations for the Negri Sembilan state election on July 16, which he said violated the coalition's constitution.
"The intention behind barring Bersatu from attending the meeting was to prevent Bersatu from contesting under the PN logo," he claimed.
"In fact, two incumbent seats held by Bersatu, namely Labu and Gemas, were allocated to Pas and Wawasan," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Many members want DAP to stay in govt, says Ngeh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Many DAP members want the party to remain in government, says its national treasurer Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham ahead of next week's national congress.
Ngeh, who is Beruas member of parliament, said feedback showed most members wanted DAP to stay in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration to fulfil the people's mandate.
"The people want us to deliver and implement good things for them. There are more advantages to being in government and serving the people than withdrawing.
"That is why I support DAP remaining with the government," he told Berita Harian in an interview.
He addressed concerns within the party that DAP should leave the government because it was no longer as vocal as before.
"But that is actually a misunderstanding. In cabinet, DAP central meetings and our dealings with the government, we remain vocal on matters that are wrong and push for them to be corrected," he said.
Ngeh said as part of the administration, DAP relies on internal channels to raise policy matters and other issues.
"So it does not mean we are no longer vocal, but the way we express our views has changed according to our position in government."
Ngeh said he raises matters through WhatsApp groups with fellow MPs and party leaders.
"However, when there is a perception that DAP has become a 'quiet' party, sometimes we need to take certain issues to the media so that the people know we are still fighting for their interests," he added.
Next week's DAP congress will see delegates decide whether the party's representatives should remain in government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 30-metre tree crashes onto car in George Town, injuring family of 3
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Three people, including a 9-year-old girl, were injured when a 30-metre Angsana tree fell onto their Perodua Ativa along Jalan Macalister this morning.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the incident, which happened around 9am, occurred in front of Tropicana 218 Macalister along the road heading towards Komtar.
"Members of the public had removed the three victims from the car before firefighters arrived," he said.
Francis said the victims were given initial treatment before being taken to Penang Hospital.
The victims were a 66-year-old man who suffered chest injuries, his 68-year-old wife who sustained injuries to her nose and left hand, and their granddaughter, 9, who suffered a hand injury.
"The operation was carried out with assistance from the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Civil Defence Force, while police and Health Ministry personnel also assisted at the scene.
The tree belonged to MBPP.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration Dept probes vehicle bearing its logo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department is investigating the unauthorised use of its logo on a vehicle driven by a foreigner after images of the vehicle went viral on social media.
Its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle was neither owned by nor an official asset of the department.
"An investigation is underway to identify the person involved and determine the purpose of using the department's logo on the vehicle.
"The department takes the misuse of its logo seriously as it could cause confusion and create a false impression among the public," he said in a statement.
Zakaria said appropriate action would be taken under existing laws if any violation was found.
He said the department would not compromise on any misuse of its logo or identity that could mislead the public or undermine its image and integrity.
The issue was earlier raised in a Threads post questioning why foreigners appeared to be driving a vehicle bearing the department's logo.
The post also questioned whether the two foreigners seen in the vehicle were authorised to drive it, describing the matter as a safety concern.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three freed after fallen tree traps them inside car in George Town
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Three people were rescued after a tree fell on the Perodua Ativa they were travelling in along Jalan Macalister this morning.
The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 9.12am and dispatched eight firefighters from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene.
“All three victims who were trapped inside the vehicle were successfully freed by members of the public before the rescue team arrived,” the department said.
Firefighters later carried out work to cut up and remove the fallen tree and debris to ensure public safety and ease traffic flow.
The department said further information on the victims’ condition would be provided when available.

Title: Malaysia awaits US response on excess capacity after concluding forced-labour tariff talks, says Johari Ghani
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 9 — Malaysia is awaiting Washington’s response on concerns over industrial excess capacity after completing the forced-labour component of its discussions with the US, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today.
The Star
reported that Johari, speaking at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia’s (ACCCIM) 80th annual general meeting here, said the government would continue engaging the US on the outstanding issue.
“We have finalised the forced-labour component. The issue of excess capacity has not been concluded yet,” he was quoted as saying.
“We are waiting for a response and will provide an update once received,” he reportedly added.
The US imposed an additional 10 per cent Section 301 tariff on Malaysian goods, subject to exemptions, from July 24 following its investigation into Malaysia’s rules on imports linked to forced labour, while a separate investigation into structural excess capacity remains unresolved.
Under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, Malaysia has committed to prohibit imports made using forced labour as well as take steps to address global excess capacity in the steel sector.
Johari also reportedly said Malaysia’s exports to the US continued to grow, but cautioned against allowing imports to rise faster and weaken the country’s trade surplus.

Title: Myanmar refugee figures soon, Saifuddin Nasution vows biometric drive for repatriation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — Preliminary data on Myanmar refugees who are currently identified through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme is expected to be obtained in the fourth quarter of this year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the Home Ministry (KDN) through the Immigration Department (JIM) is implementing the data collection process with relevant parties.
“I expect we will obtain the first data in the fourth quarter of this year, now it is August. Whatever the number is, I will share it with the media later,” he said in a press conference after the Star City FC Tour Convoy flag off ceremony here today.
The media reported that KDN through JIM is implementing the DPP programme to manage the issue of this group in an organised manner, in line with National Security Council Directive No. 23 (Revision 2023).
KDN said the programme was created to enable the government to obtain more accurate, complete and verifiable biometric data and identity information on individuals in the refugee category.
Saifuddin Nasution said individuals identified as refugees would be given priority for repatriation through action by Wisma Putra.
“If they are legitimate refugees, then they will certainly be among the first groups we will manage to repatriate. That will be handled by Wisma Putra.
“We are conducting a data collection. We need to have a mechanism to reach out to them and publicise that the Malaysian Government is conducting a data collection and we will ask them to come forward,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution explained that the refugee data collection is not focused on Myanmar refugees only but covers all those identified in this country. — Bernama

Title: 'Wishing them a speedy recovery': Anwar visits Ismail Sabri and Fadillah at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof and former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who are both receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN), yesterday.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he made the visits with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
“Azizah and I pray that both of them are granted a speedy recovery, that all aspects of their treatment are eased, and that they continue to be blessed with good health and strength to continue serving the people and the country,
insya-Allah
,” he said.
Fadillah’s office announced on August 3 that he would undergo heart bypass surgery at IJN on the advice of medical specialists, with his condition then reported to be stable.
Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, was admitted to IJN on August 6 after experiencing health issues while having his statement recorded at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission headquarters.
He underwent a successful leadless pacemaker implantation procedure for an abnormal heart rhythm the following day and remained under close monitoring at IJN.

Title: Pakatan hails BN openness, Fahmi says Melaka seat talks offer chance for stability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) welcomes the openness of Barisan Nasional (BN) regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and describes it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the openness should also be accepted for the future and political stability of Melaka, in addition to its importance to the country.
“The chairman of Keadilan Melaka, Yang Berhormat Adam Adli, also informed that he had been in direct contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof (regarding the distribution of Melaka State Legislative Assembly seats).
“I think this openness is a good opportunity for us to examine because we know that in Melaka, BN has 21 seats, while PH has five seats. So that is a realistic matter,” he told reporters after officiating the Gotong-royong Mega Perangi Aedes programme in the Lembah Pantai area, here today.
Fahmi, who is also the Communications Minister, said in this regard several matters could be managed at the state and federal levels regarding the distribution of state seats in Melaka.
Yesterday, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was still open to negotiations regarding the distribution, or even the exchange of seats, to face the Melaka state election, as long as it was done honestly and sincerely and did not affect the number of seats for each party.
Ahmad Zahid also said the basic principle of the negotiations was that the seats won by any party must be respected and not simply handed over to political partners. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution vows scanner upgrade, promises smarter baggage checks after pilot drug scandal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — The government will look into upgrading scanning machines at airports nationwide as part of efforts to strengthen security and improve the effectiveness of baggage screening, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the government was always open to exploring the use of the latest screening equipment in line with technological advancements, particularly at the country’s main entry points.
He added that the existing scanning machines at airports were functioning well and had a high capability to detect dangerous items and other prohibited materials.
“Are we going to remain static with the existing machines going forward? Certainly not, because there are various types of equipment available for airport entry-point screening that are far more advanced and have greater capabilities.
“We are always open to ideas on adopting all types of new equipment,” he said at a press conference after the flag-off ceremony for the Star City FC Tour Convoy here today.
Airport security control has come under scrutiny following several recent cases involving Malaysians, including the detention of a Malaysian pilot after about 25 kilogrammes of MDMA-type drugs were seized at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Indonesia last week.
Saifuddin Nasution said baggage screening at airports was the responsibility of the Aviation Security (AVSEC) team and was in line with international airport screening standards under the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).
In this regard, he said improvements to the scope of baggage screening were also being considered to enable prohibited items, including drugs being smuggled, to be detected.
“From the perspective of the screening scope, the focus (currently) is more on weaponry than contraband. We see this as one of the areas for improvement that we need to focus on, in line with the expertise of the officers conducting the screening,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said he and agencies under the Home Ministry would hold a special meeting tomorrow to examine the implementation of a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
