“Home Ministry and Transport Ministry have been asked to submit a comprehensive improvement plan aimed at mitigating incidents in terms of operations, equipment and manpower,” he said.
Earlier, Saifuddin Nasution said the Cabinet had instructed the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry to submit a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at KLIA within two weeks.
He said the directive followed the government’s concerns over the latest incident, which was viewed as potentially tarnishing the country’s image as well as creating a perception that there were weaknesses in the security control system at the premises. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu turns to RoS after Hadi says party automatically out of Perikatan
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) reportedly plans to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over claims that its Perikatan Nasional (PN) membership had automatically lapsed after the party expressed its intention to form a new political coalition.
Utusan Malaysia
reported Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz as saying that PN, which he claimed was now dominated by PAS, should be governed according to its constitution and principles of good governance, rather than the interests of any one party.
“PAS’ repeated actions in breaching the PN constitution and decisions of the PN Supreme Council, including denying the rights of member parties, should be reported to the RoS so that this can be stopped immediately,” he was quoted as saying.
“The PN chairman now appears to be a puppet. The centre of power is in Rusila, and the PAS president can arbitrarily question and breach decisions of the PN Supreme Council and do as he pleases.
“PN is not PAS. PN must be managed in accordance with the PN constitution, fairly, transparently and with integrity, without denying the rights of its members. PN must be restored to what it originally was,” he reportedly added.
On Friday, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang claimed Bersatu’s PN membership had automatically lapsed after its president, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, announced plans to form a new political coalition.
He said the PN constitution stipulated that a member would cease to belong to the coalition upon joining another alliance.
Bersatu, however, maintained that its position in PN remained unchanged as it had yet to decide whether to join any other political coalition, including Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR).

Title: Govt ends 40-year settlement issue with land grants for 120 Perak families, says housing minister
Article:
IPOH, Aug 9 — A total of 120 squatter families around Sungkai and Kuala Bikam have been given land grants, resolving a settlement issue they had faced for more than 40 years, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
In a statement last night, Nga said the resolution of the issue was proof that the Madani Government always prioritised the wellbeing of the people regardless of racial background and social status, in line with its commitment to ensuring no Malaysian was left behind or marginalised in development.
“The squatter problem that has dragged on for more than 40 years can finally be resolved. Last night, 120 families are receiving land grants that symbolise a more secure future for them and future generations,” he said.
The DAP national deputy chairman said this when presenting the land grants to recipients at a dinner organised by the DAP Sungkai state constituency division last night, which was attended by more than 1,200 guests from various communities.
He also expressed appreciation to Sungkai assemblyman and state Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan, as well as all civil servants who worked tirelessly and with dedication to ensure the issue was resolved.
Nga said the Madani Government's commitment to the Indian community was also reflected in various initiatives, including RM20 million allocated for Indian settlements, RM50 million for Tamil vernacular schools (SJKTs) and an increase in the allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA) to RM150 million.
“These are among the proofs that the Madani Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is constantly striving to build an inclusive, fair and equitable Malaysia, guided by the principle that no one is left behind or marginalised,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nga urged the people to assess the government's actual performance and achievements and not be swayed by racial sentiments.
“Let us not allow performance to lose out to perception. Our country needs a new, constructive politics, not an outdated, destructive one.
“The politics of the future must be rooted in unity, performance-driven service, development and the wellbeing of the people,” he said.
Also present at the DAP Sungkai 60th anniversary dinner were Ipoh Timur MP Howard Lee Chuan How, Buntong assemblyman M. Thulsi, Malim Nawar assemblyman V. Bavani, Astaka assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yong and other local community leaders. — Bernama

Title: Immigration investigates video of vehicle reportedly misusing department logo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The Immigration Department is investigating the use of its logo on a vehicle seen in a viral social media post and reportedly driven by a foreign national.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle did not belong to the department and was not one of its official assets.
“The department takes seriously the use of its logo on the vehicle as it could cause confusion and create a false impression among members of the public,” he said in a statement today.
The department said investigations were under way to identify the individual involved and determine the purpose behind the use of its logo on the vehicle.
It said appropriate action would be taken under the relevant laws if any offence was found to have been committed.
Zakaria said the department would not compromise on any misuse of its logo or identity that could mislead the public or undermine its image and integrity.
He also urged the public to exercise caution when sharing information related to the case while investigations are ongoing.

Title: Perlis Umno gears up to contest all seats solo at next election
Article:
ARAU, Aug 9 — Perlis Umno is preparing its machinery to contest all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies on its own at the next election, state liaison chairman Datuk Rozabil Abd Rahman reprotedly said.
Berita Harian
reported that Rozabil said there had so far been no official talks with any political party, including Perikatan Nasional (PN), on electoral cooperation in Perlis.
“What party members want, and what we have been working towards, is to continue working in all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies,” he was quoted as saying last night.
He said the state chapter, which failed to win any seat in Perlis at the last election, would leave any eventual decision on electoral cooperation to the party’s national leadership.
Rozabil said some parties had approached him about meeting, but he considered such discussions premature and said the immediate priority was to ensure the party machinery continued working.
He also reportedly claimed the PN state administration had failed to deliver significant development, particularly economic opportunities and jobs for young people.
He said Umno’s machinery, including Wanita Umno’s Jalinan Rakyat network at polling districts, was already being mobilised as though an election could be held at any time.

Title: Five Sarawak areas record unhealthy API levels amid transboundary haze
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 9 — Five areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am today, compared with six areas yesterday afternoon.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings were Kuching (153), Samarahan (156), Serian (170), Bintulu (156) and Samalaju (151).
Yesterday, Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas reportedly said that transboundary haze was expected to affect 19 areas in Sarawak over the next few days, with current wind patterns carrying smoke from hotspots in neighbouring regions into the state.
Uggah, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the areas identified were Betong, Bintulu, Daro, Julau, Kanowit, Kuching, Lundu, Marudi, Miri, Mukah, Pakan, Samarahan, Saratok, Serian, Sibu, Simunjan, Song, Sri Aman and Tatau. — Bernama

Title: Police track Perodua Alza occupants after passenger seen leaning out of rear window
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Police are tracking the driver and passenger of a Perodua Alza following a viral video showing the passenger sticking part of their body out of the rear window while the vehicle was moving along the Kajang-Seremban Expressway.
Kajang police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said the 12-second video went viral on Threads yesterday, with the incident believed to have occurred at KM1 of the expressway towards Kajang.
We received a report on the incident at 2.57pm yesterday, and the case is being investigated under Section 336 of the Penal Code for a rash or negligent act that endangers the life or personal safety of others,” he said in a statement last night.
He urged anyone with information on the incident to contact the nearest police station or the investigating officer, Insp Afiq Rifdi Mohd Azmi, at 011-29667474. — Bernama

Title: Man drowns while attempting to rescue eight-year-old son from Raub resort fish pond
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 9 — A man drowned while trying to save his son who had fallen into a fish pond at a resort in Sungai Ruan, Raub yesterday.
Raub District Police chief Supt Mohd Shahril Abdul Rahman said police received information on the incident involving Mohamed Hafidz Che Din, 46, at about 3pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the victim jumped into the pond to save his eight-year-old son, who had fallen in while trying to retrieve a plastic bread bag used as fishing bait.
“The victim’s son was rescued by a worker and an Indonesian national who also assisted during the incident.
“However, the victim did not resurface for about 20 minutes before he was found near the stairs at the side of the pond. He was brought out, and CPR was administered several times but to no avail,” he said when contacted last night.
Mohd Shahril said the victim was taken to Raub Hospital, where a post-mortem found that the cause of death was asphyxia secondary to drowning. — Bernama

Title: Works Ministry eyes bigger Budget 2027 allocation for development and maintenance
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Aug 9 — The Works Ministry (KKR) hopes to receive the highest development allocation among ministries in Budget 2027, to enable more development and infrastructure maintenance projects to be carried out nationwide.
Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said KKR was currently gathering input from agencies under the ministry, including the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Construction Industry Development Board Malaysia (CIDB) and Public Works Department (JKR), in preparation for Budget 2027.
He said the ministry had instructed its divisions and agencies to prepare their input last week before a meeting with Finance Minister II on August 28.
I hope KKR’s development allocation can be increased from last year. We received about RM10 billion in the previous budget, of which RM9 billion was for development,” he told reporters after the Cultural Night Run (CNR 2026) at the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah Bridge here tonight.
The event attracted 5,000 participants, including 114 from 18 countries.
Meanwhile, Ahmad said KKR, through LLM, was strengthening efforts to develop smart highways through digital technology, artificial intelligence (AI), closed-circuit television (CCTV), smart lanes and the local navigation application TuJu.
He said TuJu, developed by LLM, was Malaysia’s third navigation application after Waze and Google Maps, offering highway-specific information such as CCTV feeds, toll rates, rest and recreation (R&R) areas, emergency assistance and the latest traffic updates linked to the LLM Traffic Control Centre.
“The LLM Traffic Control Centre monitors hundreds of CCTV cameras across all 34 highways, including both bridges in Penang. TuJu is also linked to the KKR and MYJalan applications, allowing users to submit reports and complaints on road conditions,” he said.
Ahmad encouraged highway users to use TuJu for real-time traffic information to help them make better travel decisions, noting that Malaysia has 34 highways operated by 28 concessionaires, with a combined length of more than 2,000 kilometres, of which more than 1,000 kilometres are owned by PLUS Malaysia Berhad.
He said the implementation of Multi Lane Free Flow (MLFF), which enables toll collection without vehicles stopping at toll plazas, was still at the proof-of-concept (POC) stage and would be implemented through business-to-business (B2B) arrangements between concessionaires without government funding.
“The 28 concessionaires operating the 34 highways can choose either their own subsidiaries or external companies to provide the service. We have already started, with JustGo being used by PLUS as part of the MLFF initiative,” he said.
CNR2026 was organised through strategic cooperation between KKR, the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry (KUSKOP), Youth and Sports Ministry (KBS), Penang state government, Malaysia Co-operative Societies Commission (SKM), ANGKASA, Penang Amateur Athletics Association (PAAA), Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), Jambatan Kedua Sdn Bhd (JKSB), as well as various government agencies, corporate companies and other strategic partners. — Bernama

Title: Penang halts use of automatic number plate recognition for parking offences over public concerns
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — The Penang state government has instructed both local authorities in the state to immediately suspend the implementation of the Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for issuing compounds, to allow a review of its details.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was made after the state government took into account public feedback and views regarding the implementation of the system.
“The state government will instruct both local authorities, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP)) to immediately suspend the implementation of ANPR and review its details.
“What is important is that we listen to the people’s voices, review what needs to be reviewed, and ensure that every policy implemented truly takes into account the interests of the people of Penang,” he said in a Facebook post tonight.
Chow said the matter was among those discussed during a meeting with Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim and Penang DAP deputy chairman Zairil Khir Johari after he chaired the Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) Leadership Council meeting here yesterday.
Chow said they also discussed several issues concerning the livelihood of Penang residents, particularly the economic challenges currently being faced, and that several related measures would be detailed and announced in the near future.
Friday, MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the use of the ANPR system by MBPP, which began on April 24 last year, had resulted in an average of about 7,000 parking offence compounds being issued every month.
He said the number of compounds showed that the technology had helped improve the efficiency of parking enforcement, particularly as the number of parking bays managed by the local authority on the island had now reached nearly 20,000.
The ANPR system, which began operating on April 24, 2025 involving two vehicles, enabled MBPP to detect parking offences more accurately compared with manual inspection methods.
However, its implementation had caused unease and concern among Penang residents, including former Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng. — Bernama

Title: Six remanded over Alor Setar kidnapping case after police rescue two foreign nationals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Six individuals arrested to assist in investigations into the abduction of two foreign nationals in Alor Setar have been placed under remand for seven days beginning yesterday.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects comprise a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, who were arrested in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur.
“All six have been remanded until August 14 to facilitate investigations,” he said when contacted yesterday.
Friday, two men believed to be foreign nationals were shot dead in an exchange of fire with police during an operation to rescue the two kidnapping victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata in Alor Setar at about 8.40pm.
The operation also saw the rescue of the two victims - a foreign man in his 70s and a foreign woman in her 30s - who were found blindfolded and handcuffed.
The case is being investigated under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, which deals with kidnapping for ransom. — Bernama

Title: Anwar hails AKPS for seizing suspected Israel-bound shipment at Johor port
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his appreciation to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) for its swift action in seizing a container suspected of carrying strategic goods for export to Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor Friday.
In a post on Facebook yesterday, he said the action demonstrated Malaysia’s firmness in ensuring that the country does not become a transit route for trade that could support or contribute to the Israeli regime’s atrocities against the Palestinian people.
“It is also in line with Malaysia’s commitment under The Hague Group, as well as the ban that has been in effect since December 2023 prohibiting Israeli ships and vessels carrying cargo to Israel from using the country’s ports,” he said.
Anwar said Malaysia would continue to uphold the principles of humanity, justice and international law in defending the rights and dignity of the Palestinian people.
Earlier, AKPS said in a statement that it had detained and inspected a container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas Friday that was suspected of carrying goods for export to Israel.
According to the agency, the shipment was suspected of violating Item No. 15 of the Second Schedule of the Customs (Prohibition of Exports) Order 2023, which prohibits the direct or indirect export of goods to Israel in accordance with the policies and directives of the Malaysian government. — Bernama

Title: Penang woodcarver keeps age-old craft alive as demand grows (VIDEO)
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — For more than two decades, Lee Chee Cheng has turned plain planks into ornate signboards bearing gilded Chinese characters, dragons,
qilin
and other symbols of prosperity.
The 63-year-old proprietor of Sung Dynasty Wood Carving learned the traditional craft from his late uncle, who had operated from Air Itam, before eventually taking over the trade.
“I learned from my uncle for several years. Before that, I worked in sales, selling books and cars,” he said in an interview with
Malay Mail.
Labour of love
Lee said he had initially resisted entering the labour-intensive trade when he was younger, choosing instead to work in other industries.
“You know how it is, when you are young, you want to do other things, you don’t want to be involved in manual work that seemed tedious,” he said.
However, when the economy slowed in 1997, it was a difficult time for his sales job so he began helping his uncle during his days off.
“I began to see the value in the trade then but I was still working at that time so I only helped out whenever I have time,” he said.
That was when he slowly learned the trade from his uncle.
Lee Chee Cheng showing the traditional Chinese name stamps that he also makes. — Picture by Opalyn Mok
The family business
“When my uncle passed away, the family asked if I wanted to take over and since I realised my sales job was going nowhere, I decided to take over and give it a try,” he said.
That saw the birth of Sung Dynasty Wood Carving about 20 years ago, first being based in Air Itam before relocating to its current premises in Carnavon Street about 10 years ago.
“I named it Sung Dynasty because that was the era known for its artisans and craftsmen,” he said.
He said the early years of the business were difficult, with few customers and orders and he was running at a loss in the first year.
“It was because I was new in the industry so it was not easy to get customers to trust my work,” he said.
Steady demand
However, as the years go by, Lee started to gain more customers, most of whom are temples, associations and businesses.
“Business started improving about 10 years ago so finally, I was able to break even and earn a good income,” he said.
Today, his business is stable and he no longer has to worry about covering costs such as rental and utility bills.
“Now I worry about whether I can meet all the orders,” he said.
Lee Chee Cheng took over the wood carving business from his uncle over 20 years ago. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
Attention to craft
Other than making new signboards, Lee also restores damaged antique deity statues and signboards.
“If the signboard was too damaged, I would have to make a new one for them but if it’s an antique, I find a way to restore it,” he said.
In addition to signboards, Lee also carve wooden altars and traditional Chinese name stamps.
“I work alone on most orders so that’s why I worry I am not able to meet customers’ orders on time but I do have an assistant who helps to carve the name stamps,” he said.
Despite working alone, Lee takes between four to five days to produce one signboard.
“The whole process is quite straightforward, I coat it first, then draw in the designs, carve out the motifs and after that I spray paint it either black or red, according to the customer’s requirement,” he said.
He said it takes a day for the paint to dry and once it’s fully dried, the last step was to apply gold leaf on the wordings, which is usually the name of the business, association or temple.
Lee Chee Cheng working on the handcarved wooden signboards. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
Faithful clientele
Lee said fewer people were entering the trade, which has led to more customers seeking his services for wooden signboards for businesses, temples and occasionally homes.
“These are what we called kam chee chiu pai (golden-word signboards) as the wordings are always in gold,” he said.
As for the designs, he said the placement of the wordings and motifs such as the flowers and mythical creatures like dragons and qilin must follow traditional conventions.
“I can’t simply decide to draw a durian on it, these signboards that are placed on the front of the premises must have auspicious motifs in accordance with tradition and culture,” he said.
While Lee said wood carving is not a trade that will make someone rich, he believes it is a specialised tradition that should be continued.
“With this kind of handicraft, you will not become rich, but you will not be unemployed either,” he said.
“At my age, I can accept that. Compared to working elsewhere, this is better for me. It is a craft,” he added.
A visit to Sung Dynasty Wood Carving at Carnavon Street with the proprietor Lee Chee Cheng. — Picture courtesy of Penang Global Tourism
Passing on the torch
Lee’s children are not interested in taking over the business as they have their own careers but he is not opposed to teaching his trade to the younger generation.
“I will be teaching others interested in this craft under the Penang Heritage Trust’s Penang Apprenticeship Programme for Artisan (PAPA) programme,” he said.
He had even prepared the basic materials such as small wooden boards for the training programme.
Lee was among 10 traditional trades featured in Penang Global Tourism’s traditional trades campaign this year, held in collaboration with Penang Heritage Trust.
The campaign was presented for the second time following its successful debut last year and was recently launched by state tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai.
The other nine traditional trades featured are Ong Chin Chye the joss stick maker, SM Badjenid and Sons, Jeruk Madu Pak Ali, San Kwan Loong Soy Sauce Factory, Eng Seng Kuih Kapit, Yeoh Siong Huat bedak sejuk maker, Teochew opera, Raju Murugesan the goldsmith and Kenny Loh the kebaya designer.

Title: Experts urge holistic measures, warn teacher workload threatens mental health and classroom quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The issue of teacher workload needs to be addressed holistically and continuously through strengthening the scope of work and providing a sustainable support system to ensure that the mental and physical well-being of educators continues to be maintained.
In this regard, measures to streamline administrative tasks, increase teaching staff and provide a sustainable support system are critical to ensure that the physical and mental well-being of the group does not continue to be neglected.
Senior Lecturer at the Faculty of Educational Sciences and Technology, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Dr Mohammad Faiz Ikhlas said teacher workload does exist and is due, among other things, to filling in too much data, an unstable online data entry system, student discipline issues and assignment instructions outside of working hours.
He said the pressure to achieve school performance targets often forces teachers to ‘steal’ breaks until late at night, thus affecting the quality of their personal and family lives.
“Some teachers experience emotional stress, fear, and some even experience fatigue or burnout. It also directly affects the quality of their teaching and personal lives,” he told Bernama.
Mohammad Faiz said that among other factors contributing to stress are external tasks such as training students for competitions on weekends, in addition to financial constraints that force teachers to find their own funds to ensure school participation.
Commenting on the recent incident involving the death of a teacher, he suggested that the issue of workload be given serious attention and praised the move by the Ministry of Education (MOE) to limit school opening meetings to a maximum of two days starting from the 2026 session.
He said other initiatives such as the appointment of examination invigilators from among the public, the abolition of low-impact events and the granting of autonomy in Classroom Assessment (PBD) were the right steps to reduce the burden on this group.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Faiz said efforts to reduce teachers’ load must be accompanied by concrete and long-term measures, including expanding the appointment of teaching assistants based on school needs and increasing the recruitment of new teachers to fill vacancies.
Meanwhile, deputy director of the Malaysian Inclusive Development and Advancement Institute (MINDA), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), Dr Anuar Ahmad stressed that it is time for the Ministry of Education to gazette the scope of teachers’ duties clearly according to position and grade.
“It is time for the Ministry of Education to gazette what the scope of a teacher’s duties actually is so that teachers are clear about the scope of their duties,” he said.
Anuar said that reducing the workload also needs to be implemented in stages, including reducing the number of students in classes, increasing teacher staff and providing a more efficient support system in schools.
He said that clarifying the scope of teachers’ duties is not only important for educators, but also needs to be understood by schools, District Education Offices (PPDs), parents and the community so that teachers can return to focusing on teaching and learning and interacting with students.
“If teachers are burdened with non-teaching duties, they are burdened and teachers’ well-being will also be affected, and the end result will be on our students,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina hails Nadi Mahir school uniform instalment plan easing parents’ burden, empowering entrepreneurs
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 8 — The National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) Mahir initiative, enabling parents to purchase school uniforms on an instalment plan, is helping to ease their financial burden.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said in addition to making it easier for families to obtain school necessities, the initiative also creates income opportunities and empowers local entrepreneurs under Nadi’s guidance.
“As the Member of Parliament for Nibong Tebal, I see this as an excellent programme for the people,” she told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita programme in Nibong Tebal today.
Also present were Ministry of Communications (Telecommunications Infrastructure) deputy secretary-general Mano Verabathran and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission State Affairs chief officer Bukhari Yahya.
The school uniforms are sewn by 120 alumni of the Nadi Mahir Jahit programme, who had undergone skills training through its Pintar Services and are now successful entrepreneurs.
Elaborating further, Fadhlina said various initiatives implemented through Nadi have directly benefited the community, including the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat, e-sports, skills training and entrepreneurship programmes.
Over 42,000 students nationwide have joined the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat programme, with more than 73 from Nibong Tebal. The programme produced 65 outstanding students in the 2025 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examination.
She said youth involvement through Nadi E-Sukan is a platform to uncover talent and boost confidence and teamwork among young people.
She noted that Nadi’s achievements in Nibong Tebal include winning the national Nadi E-Sukan Madani Mobile Legends title, finishing as runners-up at the Penang state level, and placing second in the Penang state-level Cooking Star competition.
Nadi also provides exposure to AI through various programmes, including the 1 Nadi 1 Prompt Engineer initiative, which has so far attracted 11 participants in Nibong Tebal. — Bernama

Title: Chow stresses Penang Pakatan unity, BN exco retained as coalition eyes next GE
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 8 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) has decided to retain the Barisan Nasional (BN) state executive councillor in the state administration until the next general election (GE), said its chairman Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the decision was reached at the Penang PH meeting today based on the electoral pact between PH and BN formed during the 2023 state election.
“In facing the next GE, we believe there is still room to strengthen cooperation among the component parties and accelerate the reform agenda that forms the basis of PH’s struggle,” he told a press conference after chairing the Penang PH meeting at Wisma DAP here today.
The BN executive councillor is State Rural Development, Agrotechnology and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.
Chow, who is also Chief Minister, said Penang PH had also taken lessons from the results of the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, with every seat in the state to be analysed from various perspectives ahead of the 16th GE.
He said PH would also strengthen its political narrative by acknowledging its weaknesses, making more effective use of digital platforms and engaging more closely with the growing Undi18 voter group.
Chow said the coalition remained confident in its strength, citing the state administration’s stability and integrity, as well as its efforts to drive economic growth, attract investments, create jobs and implement policies benefiting the people.
However, he said the coalition could not afford to be complacent about its performance, as public perceptions and sentiments often changed faster than facts.
In the 2023 Penang state election, PH and BN formed the Unity Government after winning 29 of the 40 state seats contested, with DAP winning all 19 seats it contested, PKR seven, Amanah one and BN two. — Bernama

Title: Seat swaps possible in Melaka, Zahid says negotiations must remain fair and principled
Article:
KUDAT, Aug 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) remains open to negotiations on seat allocations for the Melaka State Election, including seat swaps, provided they are conducted honestly and in good faith, said BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The Deputy Prime Minister said the basic principle of the negotiations was that seats won by any party must be respected and should not simply be handed over to political partners.
“As I have stated, the Melaka Chief Minister (Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh), who is also the Melaka BN chairman, said that as a matter of principle, in any negotiations, the position of any party that has won a seat must be respected.
“But negotiations can be held for a ‘swap’ or exchange of seats, provided the number of seats remains the same,” he told a press conference after officiating the Rungus Cultural Festival here today.
Ahmad Zahid said seat swaps could also be negotiated involving other states controlled by the respective parties, provided the exchanges were carried out in a balanced manner.
“Our principle is that it is not impossible for the door to remain open for negotiations, but do not open it too wide and do not shut it completely,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Shrimp import talks with Thailand at final stage, resolution expected by mid‑August, says Mat Sabu
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 8 — Discussions on the issue of shrimp imports from Thailand are at the final stage and are expected to be resolved by mid-August, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
“A resolution is expected to be reached within that timeframe,” he told reporters after attending the closing of the Road to MAHA 2026 East Coast Zone programme here today.
The ministry announced last month that it had temporarily suspended imports of five shrimp species from Thailand effective June 1 as part of stricter controls on fishery products from the neighbouring country.
The species are
Penaeus esculentus
(brown tiger shrimp),
Fenneropenaeus merguiensis
(banana shrimp),
Penaeus vannamei
(white shrimp),
Penaeus monodon
(tiger shrimp) and
Penaeus stylirostris
(blue shrimp).
Meanwhile, Mohamad said MAHA 2026 would focus on innovation and modernisation in the agriculture sector, with participation from more countries, including those from Africa and Central Asia, as well as China, Britain, Japan and the United States.
He said the participation reflected interest in agricultural technology developments and would provide opportunities for technology-sharing between countries.
“Food security is now a major agenda worldwide, especially for a country like Malaysia, which still relies heavily on food imports,” he said.
Mohamad said the Road to MAHA 2026 programme in Kota Bharu was the final instalment after similar programmes were held in Kedah, Selangor, Melaka and Labuan.
He also expressed appreciation to the state government, federal and state government agencies, and strategic partners for their cooperation in making the programme a success.
Mohamad said he was confident MAHA 2026 could attract around five million visitors, similar to the number recorded two years ago, with the National Day celebrations also expected to draw more visitors.
MAHA 2026, scheduled from August 28 to September 6, targets four million visitors, RM58 million in sales and RM8 billion in potential investments, while showcasing modern agricultural technology, innovation and industry cooperation. — Bernama

Title: Perak Education Department vows fair handling of Chemor teacher bullying complaint, welfare prioritised
Article:
IPOH, Aug 8 — The school administration and the teacher who recently alleged that she was bullied and subjected to psychological pressure need to work together to resolve the matter in the interest of the pupils.
Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said both parties should adopt a conciliatory approach in resolving the matter instead of blaming each other.
“The matter has been brought to my attention, and we have asked the District Education Office and the Perak Education Department to investigate the allegations.
“The investigation has been completed and I have also received the full report, with the findings as stated in the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA),” he told reporters after opening the Todak Academy (Perak) Digital Education Hub here today.
Yesterday, it was reported that a teacher at a school in Chemor had alleged that she was subjected to bullying, intimidation and emotional distress at the workplace between March and May.
Khairudin said he was not blaming either party, stressing that all actions should be taken in accordance with the processes and procedures set by the Ministry of Education.
“I am not blaming either party because both have their own arguments and evidence. The school administration is bound by certain circulars and procedures, while the teacher involved also needs to understand that every action must follow the prescribed process,” he said.
On the teacher’s claim that she had suffered seizures, he said the matter needed to be confirmed by the medical officer handling the case.
“The matter needs to be confirmed by a doctor. I understand that the teacher has sought treatment, so let us wait for the medical report and not make any assumptions,” he said.
Meanwhile, Perak Education director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said in a statement that the Perak Education Department (JPN) had taken note of the issue which went viral on social media.
He said department took all complaints seriously and remained committed to ensuring that every complaint was handled professionally and transparently, in accordance with the regulations and procedures in force, while safeguarding the welfare of teachers.
He also said that the Perak JPN, together with the District Education Office (PPD), had taken follow-up action since March 2026, including engagement sessions, reviews, monitoring and coordination with the relevant parties to ensure that every matter raised received due attention.
“Perak JPN will continue to prioritise the welfare and well-being of all parties involved, while ensuring that harmony in the school environment and the smooth operation of educational institutions are maintained.
“Perak JPN remains committed to handling every complaint fairly, with integrity and accountability, in the best interests of the education community,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Police seek owner, motive behind pink suitcase left at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS after explosive scare
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Aug 8 — Police have opened an investigation paper to identify the owner and determine why a suitcase was left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex (ICQS), after a scan detected images resembling explosives and drugs.
Kedah Police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said preliminary investigations found that the spot where the suitcase was left was outside CCTV coverage, making it difficult for police to identify the individual who left it there.
“Police are currently investigating to identify the owner of the suitcase as well as the reason it was left at the location,” he told reporters here today.
Yesterday, police had carried out a process to neutralise a pink suitcase left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS.
The suitcase was then taken to a scanning machine, and the scan showed images indicating the presence of suspected drugs and explosive materials.
The Bomb Disposal Unit of the Kedah Police Contingent headquarters, which carried out the process to neutralise the suitcase, found no explosive materials and only discovered clothes, oil in a container, a black hairdryer, shampoo and lotion. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin: Selangor govt to meet Panasonic workers over jobs, assistance after planned closure
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 8 — The Selangor state government will meet workers expected to be affected by the closure of television production operations at Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PAVCKM) next week to discuss assistance and alternative employment opportunities.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting would be conducted by State Human Resources, Poverty Alleviation, Indigenous & Minority Affairs Committee chairman V. Papparaidu, together with representatives from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), to obtain relevant information from the affected workers.
“Next week, Papparaidu will meet with the affected group to explore and offer necessary support, especially as their factory faces potential closure.
“Early intervention measures, such as providing food baskets, will certainly be carried out, but we will also assist them in finding alternative employment so they can sustain the lives they have built in this state over the years,” he told reporters after officiating the Selangor Mega Jobcare 2026 programme here today.
In a statement yesterday, Panasonic Malaysia Sdn Bhd (Panasonic) said production operations for two products would be closed, impacting 400 workers by the end of March next year.
Meanwhile, Papparaidu said cooperation with Perkeso could see the agency providing financial protection and assistance to workers who lose their jobs amid the expected retrenchments.
“The most important part is Perkeso providing a form of insurance where, if they are retrenched and remain unemployed, they will receive payments in stages. It acts as a job-seeking allowance, starting at 80 per cent of their salary in the first month, 50 per cent in the second month, and subsequently 30 per cent as well.
“This is a new initiative by Perkeso that greatly assists people, especially Selangor residents who face retrenchment. I hope we do our best to resolve these issues,” he said.
Meanwhile, Selangor Mega Jobcare 2026 brings together 147 employers offering more than 11,000 vacancies, with 62.2 per cent offering monthly salaries exceeding RM3,000.
The career fair, organised in collaboration with MYFutureJobs for participants aged between 18 and 60, is being held at the Shah Alam Convention Centre (SACC) from 9 am to 5 pm and concludes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: AADK backs mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, cabin crew
Article:
JERTIH, Aug 8 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) supports the move by Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) to make it compulsory for 1,260 Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilots to undergo drug screening following the recent arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia.
AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move to tighten security controls and extend mandatory drug screening to all active pilots and cabin crew members was in line with the zero-tolerance policy towards drug abuse and trafficking.
“Safety in the aviation sector cannot be compromised because this industry bears a great responsibility for the lives of thousands of passengers,” he said after officiating the AADK’s Madani Foster Village (KAM) and Madani Foster School (SAM) programmes at Felda Tenang here today.
He said the AADK is ready to cooperate with MAG through drug abuse detection operations, strengthening the Drug-Free Workplace (TEKAD) programme, screening and prevention training for supervisors as well as cross-agency cooperation.
Ruslin said AADK had previously conducted drug abuse detection operations involving flight crew, including at MAS in April 2025 and AirAsia in December 2025.
“AADK will continue to work with the police, Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and international regulatory bodies to strengthen information sharing and security controls at all the country’s main entry points,” he said.
While acknowledging that isolated actions by individuals should not tarnish the image and professionalism of the majority of the country’s dedicated aviation workforce, Ruslin reaffirmed AADK’s commitment to support government and private sector efforts to ensure Malaysia remains free from the threat of drugs.
Meanwhile, he said the implementation of the KAM and SAM programmes at Felda Tenang demonstrated that rural development should not only focus on physical infrastructure, but also include efforts to build human capital that is safe, prosperous and free from drugs.
He said the facilities which were upgraded included the football field pavilion, futsal and sepak takraw courts, Dewan Nurul Ehsan, solar lighting at the cemetery, as well as school learning facilities such as covered walkways, air-conditioning and public address systems.
He said the number of drug addicts and drug abusers in Terengganu fell 7.2 per cent to 7,582 people in the first quarter of 2026 from 8,174 during the same period last year.
“However, the 16.7 per cent increase in involvement among children aged 10 to 14, as well as rising number of cases among those aged 55 to 59 and 65 to 69, is quite worrying,” he said.
He said young people need to be given special attention, with SAM serving as one of the early lines of defence against drug abuse at the school and community levels.
Rusliln said Amphetamine-Type Stimulants (ATS), such as syabu (methamphetamine), yaba pills and ecstasy, remained the most prevalent, accounting for 6,206 cases or 81.9 per cent, followed by opiates with 1,281 cases or 16.9 per cent in the first quarter of this year.
He also called on AADK, Felda, educators, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), youth and the local community to strengthen cooperation to ensure Felda Tenang and Besut continue to develop with quality infrastructure and remain free from the threat of drugs. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji recovery plan addressed RM12.6b losses but further reforms needed, says RCI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) restructuring and recovery plan successfully restored the institution’s financial position after addressing RM12.6 billion in investment losses, while further reforms are needed to ensure its long-term sustainability, according to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI).
The fully declassified report said RM10 billion of the losses was addressed under the 2018 Recovery Plan, while the remaining RM2.6 billion was resolved progressively through the end of 2025.
It also noted that 75 per cent of its recommendations had been implemented, with the government committed to expediting the remaining 25 per cent as part of ongoing efforts to strengthen governance, investment discipline and risk management.
The effectiveness of the recovery measures was reflected in TH’s improved financial performance, with investment income reaching RM4.64 billion last year, its highest since 2018.
The commission nevertheless stressed that despite the progress achieved, several structural issues must still be addressed to safeguard TH’s long-term sustainability.
A key component of the recovery plan was the transfer of TH’s underperforming assets to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), a government-owned special purpose vehicle (SPV), enabling the institution to refocus on its core mandate, particularly the management of haj operations.
The assets were transferred at RM19.9 billion, compared with their market value of RM9.7 billion at the time, representing a premium of RM10.2 billion.
The commission concluded that the transfer preserved TH’s financial position and described the restructuring and recovery plan as instrumental in resolving the institution’s financial crisis.
However, it cautioned that the plan should not be regarded as a long-term solution, identifying several critical issues that remain unresolved.
These include strengthening corporate governance, reviewing the Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535), enhancing risk management and cost controls, and introducing a regulatory framework to ensure TH remains resilient.
Among the commission’s principal concerns was the government’s ability to redeem UJSB sukuk and continue providing the annual cash allocations previously promised by the Cabinet.
It warned that failure to do so could result in continued profit distributions to depositors without adequate cash backing.
Separately, TH had previously explained that the transfer of its underperforming assets to UJSB was financed through two sukuk issuances backed by government letters of support, carrying annual profit rates of 4.05 per cent and 4.10 per cent.
The institution also said UJSB had made several offers over the years to sell assets back to TH, although none met the institution’s investment criteria at the time.
Following a fresh review this year, however, TH repurchased land at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) for RM270 million, compared with the original transfer price of RM400 million.
TH also repurchased the UJ Estates (Holdings) Sdn Bhd oil palm plantation for RM695 million, below its original transfer price of RM800 million.
The institution’s recovery has also been reflected in its annual profit distribution, which rose from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.25 per cent in 2024 and 3.5 per cent in 2025.
TH said the distributions were declared after taking into account RM2.6 billion in impaired assets that could not be transferred to UJSB at the end of 2018 for specific reasons.
It added that its financial position was now significantly stronger and that it had begun rebuilding reserves to support its long-term financial sustainability.
The RCI concluded that while the restructuring and recovery plan had successfully stabilised TH’s financial position, sustained reforms in governance, regulation and risk management remain essential to safeguard the institution’s future resilience. — Bernama

Title: Anwar pledges thorough probe into every Tabung Haji RCI finding following King’s decree
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The government has pledged to investigate every recommendation thoroughly and the findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
In a Facebook post today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was in line with the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring a comprehensive investigation into the report.
“I humbly thank His Majesty for granting me an audience to brief him on several important developments concerning the country’s interests and the wellbeing of the people.
“His Majesty’s order for a thorough investigation into the RCI report reflects the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring that every recommendation and finding is fully investigated without compromise,” he said.
Anwar said the matter was among several key developments discussed during his more than hour-long audience with Sultan Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku here today.
He said TH manages a trust built from the hard-earned savings of millions of Malaysians, including farmers, civil servants and middle- and lower-income earners who have spent years saving to perform the haj pilgrimage.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said there could be no betrayal of such a significant trust, and those found to have misused it must be held accountable under the law.
The RCI report on TH, published on July 29, detailed various findings concerning weaknesses in the institution’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
The Prime Minister also briefed the King on developments in the investigation into Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA), saying the government was reviewing the special task force report to determine the appropriate action in accordance with the law.
Anwar said the Madani government remained steadfast in upholding good governance, transparency and accountability, with no one who betrayed the people’s trust spared from firm action, regardless of position or rank.
He said the government would continue to reinforce security controls at the country’s entry points through effective enforcement, continuous surveillance and close inter-agency cooperation to tackle cross-border crime while protecting national security and sovereignty.
“Insya-Allah, I and the entire government will remain committed to His Majesty’s decree to strengthen governance, enforcement and national security, while ensuring the wellbeing of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MACC, police and IRB ramp up investigations into alleged Tabung Haji irregularities after RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Enforcement agencies have stepped up action following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution.
By yesterday, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had remanded five individuals to assist in investigations into various alleged misconduct uncovered in the 211-page report released on July 29.
Those remanded for between three and five days comprised individuals from various professional backgrounds, including a former plantation manager, a design company director, a deputy general manager for construction, an occupational safety and health manager, and a project director of a statutory body’s property company.
Separately, the MACC Special Task Force detained the former chief executive officer (CEO) and former chief financial officer (CFO) of a statutory body on Aug 4 to facilitate investigations into alleged abuse of power involving a RM370 million share acquisition involving two plantation companies.
However, both suspects, aged 68 and 60, were released due to health reasons. The former CFO completed giving his statement yesterday, while the former CEO remains on medical leave.
Meanwhile, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), through its Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), has opened five investigation papers following nine reports lodged by TH, its subsidiaries and members of the public.
CCID director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said investigators were in the process of recording statements from witnesses in Malaysia and abroad, as well as obtaining relevant documents to complete the investigations.
The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has also begun investigating several individuals after detecting significant discrepancies between their ownership of luxury assets and their declared income.
It said its tax risk analysis had uncovered inconsistencies in the individuals’ income declarations, prompting raids at several premises to seize documents and verify facts relevant to the investigations.
The RCI report, which examined TH’s operations between 2014 and 2020, highlighted numerous governance weaknesses and alleged excessive political interference in profit distribution and haj operations.
Among the report’s most striking findings was that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion for the 2017 financial year, but instead reported an extraordinary profit of RM3.4 billion in its financial statements.
Following severe asset impairment, the report recommended forensic audits into several high-risk investment decisions involving PT TH Indo Plantations, Emrail Sdn Bhd, Wellspring Worldwide Limited, Abraj Sdn Bhd, Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, TH Plantations Bhd, TH Properties Sdn Bhd, Alam Maritim Resources/TH Marine, TH Hotel & Residences Sdn Bhd and FGV Bhd, which allegedly resulted in substantial losses to depositors’ funds.
It also proposed several measures, including recovering RM2.19 million in bonuses paid to TH Properties’ board members and management after finding that the payments did not comply with established regulations.
The report further described bonus payments equivalent to between two and 13 months’ salary awarded to TH staff between 2010 and 2017 as excessive and unjustifiable given the institution’s financial position during that period.
The findings and recommendations are expected to come under scrutiny during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting scheduled for Aug 11 to debate the RCI report.
On Aug 5, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said between 35 and 40 MPs had expressed interest in participating in the special sitting. — Bernama
